docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

Each term is defined once here and used with this meaning in every customer document.

Term Meaning Admin console The web pages where your administrators change settings, see who holds a seat, install the licence and read the change history. It is part of your own installation, at /admin/ on the connector's address. Administrator A person who can sign in to the admin console. A full administrator can change everything; a read-only person can look but not change. Agent A person who takes and places calls from GoHighLevel. Each agent has a GoHighLevel user and an Amazon Connect user. Agent mapping The list on the server that links each agent's GoHighLevel email address to their Amazon Connect user name. Only mapped agents get a call panel. Amazon Connect Amazon's cloud contact centre service. It carries the calls. Your organisation owns the Amazon Connect instance. Amazon Q (Q in Connect) The Amazon Connect assistant that suggests answers during a call and answers questions typed into Ask Q. Approved origin An address that Amazon Connect allows to show its softphone. The connector's address must be on this list. Audit log The server's record of security-relevant events (sign-ins, setting changes, seat changes). It holds ids only, never personal details. Authenticator app A phone app (for example Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or 1Password) that shows a new six-digit code every 30 seconds. Used to sign in to the admin console. Call entry The "Call completed" item the connector creates in the contact's conversation in GoHighLevel. Call panel The panel the connector adds to every GoHighLevel page. It shows the call controls, the caller, and the Assist, Transcript and Summary tabs. When folded away it is a small mini bar at the right edge. Confirm it is you A fresh check (authenticator code or passkey) the admin console asks for before sensitive changes. Connector The server program your organisation runs. It joins GoHighLevel and Amazon Connect, writes the call records and serves the call panel and the admin console. Contact Lens The Amazon Connect feature that produces the live transcript, caller sentiment and the AI call summary. Disposition The outcome an agent chooses after a call, for example "Interested" or "Wrong number". GoHighLevel (GHL) The CRM your agents work in. Grace period Days after a paid licence ends during which calls keep working, so a late renewal does not stop the team. Trial licences have none. Licence A signed text file from OctaveBytes that says how many seats you may use and until when. It is checked by your connector on its own, without contacting OctaveBytes. Passkey A sign-in method that uses your device's lock (Touch ID, Windows Hello, a phone or a security key) instead of a code. It needs the connector to have a domain name and HTTPS. Platform The part of the connector that adds the licence, seats, settings and the admin console. It is switched on with PLATFORM=on on the server. Recording player The audio player shown in the call entry. It plays the Amazon Connect recording for people signed in to Amazon Connect with permission to hear recordings. Recovery code A one-use code for signing in to the admin console when you have lost your phone or passkey. You get ten at setup. Screen pop The connector opening the caller's contact in GoHighLevel when a call rings. Seat One open softphone window. The licence limits how many can be open at the same time. A seat is taken whatever the agent's status is, including Offline. Setup code A one-time code that lets a new administrator create their sign-in. It works once and expires after 24 hours. Softphone The Amazon Connect phone that runs in the softphone window, a separate browser window the agent opens from the call panel and keeps open. Wrap-up The step after a call where the agent chooses a disposition and adds a note before the call is finished.

docs.title: Admin guide
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

For the people who run the connector day to day. Use the console to change settings, watch seats, install the licence and manage who can sign in. The admin console exists only when the platform is switched on (see the installation guide).

The console header, passkey prompts and your authenticator app show the product name, "GHL CTI Connector for Amazon Connect". Authenticator entries made on an earlier release show the old name, "Amazon Connect for GoHighLevel". They keep working. Screenshots in this guide were taken with a demonstration product and show "Demo Product" in the header and different settings. The layout is the same.

docs.title: Where the console is
docs.text: At /admin/ on your connector's address, for example https://cti.example.com/admin/. It works in any current browser, also at phone width, and follows your device's light or dark setting (the Auto / Light / Dark button at the bottom of the menu changes it).

docs.title: 1. First sign-in with a setup code
docs.text:
Your installer runs a command on the server that prints a setup code for you. It works once and expires after 24 hours.

  1. Open /admin/, choose I have a setup code, enter the code and press Continue.
  2. On "Welcome", add at least one way to sign in. There are no passwords.
  3. Authenticator app: scan the QR code with an authenticator app (for example Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or 1Password), or type the key shown under "Cannot scan it?", then type the six digits the app shows.
  4. Passkey (recommended): press Add a passkey and use Touch ID, Windows Hello, your phone or a security key. This option appears only when the console has a domain name and HTTPS.
  5. Press Finish setup.
  6. "Your recovery codes": ten codes, each usable once, shown only now. Press Copy the codes or write them down, store them somewhere safe (a password manager), tick I have saved these codes and press Open the console.

docs.title: 2. Signing in
docs.text:
• Passkey: type your email address and press Sign in with a passkey.
  • Authenticator app: type your email address and the six-digit code, then Sign in with the code. The email address is needed: a code on its own is treated as an unknown account.
  • Lost phone: open I lost my phone, type your email address and one recovery code, Sign in with a recovery code. Then make new codes or set up a new phone on My sign-in.

If sign-in fails you see "Sign-in failed. Check the details and try again, or wait a few minutes." The same message is used for every failure, so it does not reveal which part was wrong. Check: the email address, the right entry in the authenticator app (each system you use has its own entry), and that your phone's clock is set automatically. Five failures lock the account for 15 minutes.

Your session ends after 30 minutes without activity, and after 8 hours at most. Settings you saved stay in effect. Agents are not affected.

Confirm it is you. Some actions ask for a fresh code or your passkey if your last check was more than 10 minutes ago: installing a licence, inviting, changing or removing administrators, changing sign-in methods, and ending the session of an agent who is on a call.

docs.title: 3. The pages
docs.text: The menu has two groups. Settings: Calling, Wrap-up, Conversation logging, AI assist, Advanced. Manage: Agents, Licence, Change history, Administrators, My sign-in. Read-only people see every page but cannot change anything ("You have read-only access. Ask an administrator to change settings.").

docs.title: 4. Settings
docs.text:
Each settings page lists switches, lists and choices with a short explanation. Every setting is enforced by the server, not only hidden on screen. The full list with keys, defaults and where each is enforced is in the settings reference. The summary below says what each page is for.

How saving works - Changes are drafts until you save. Changed rows are marked, the menu shows a dot on pages with unsaved changes, and a bar at the bottom says "N unsaved changes. Nothing changes for your agents until you save." with Discard and Save changes. - After saving, "Changes saved" appears and the page shows "All changes saved". - If you try to log out with unsaved changes you are asked "Log out without saving?". The browser also warns before closing the page. - If another administrator saved a change to the same setting meanwhile, you see "Someone else saved changes while you were editing. Review them below, then save again." with Use theirs and Keep mine on each affected row. - A saved change reaches every open call panel at once. A call in progress keeps the settings it started with. - A setting indented under another has no effect while the one above it is off. Settings marked Planned cannot be switched on in this release.

Calling. Decide whether agents can place calls and pick the outbound queue, whether the contact opens when a call rings, which in-call controls appear (Hold and resume, Keypad, Mute) and whether missed calls are recorded. Transfer is Planned.

Figure: The Calling settings page.

Wrap-up. Turn the wrap-up step on or off, show or require a disposition and a note, and keep the disposition lists for inbound and outbound calls. To edit a list, type in "Add an entry" and press Add, or remove an entry with its ×. Up to 30 entries of up to 40 characters. Removing an entry affects future calls only.

Figure: The Wrap-up page with one unsaved change; nothing changes for agents until Save changes.

The shipped lists are Interested, Callback requested, Not interested, No answer, Wrong number, Other, with no disposition required. If you want longer lists or a required disposition, set them here and press Save changes.

Conversation logging. What is written to GoHighLevel after each call: the "Call completed" entry and its recording player, the transcript comment, and the note with its optional parts (AI summary, recording link, disposition).

Figure: The Conversation logging page.

AI assist. Live Amazon Q suggestions, the live transcript and the AI call summary. Switching one off also hides its tab in the call panel. "Suggest a disposition" is Planned.

Figure: The AI assist page, with the Planned switch locked.

Advanced. Connector switched on is the master switch. Off removes every call panel within about a minute and refuses new softphone sign-ins. Calls in progress finish and are logged. The page also sets the starting view of the call panel (full or compact), whether the contact page refreshes after a call is saved, and whether contacts are created for unknown callers.

Figure: The Advanced page.

Before switching anything off that changes what is stored, check with whoever owns your records policy.

docs.title: 5. Agents
docs.text:
"Who is signed in right now. This list updates by itself."

  • The seat meter shows "N of M seats in use" with a note: seats free, "Nearly full", "All seats are in use. The next agent to sign in is told no seat is free.", or, if more people are signed in than the licence allows (for example after a smaller licence was installed), how many are over. People over the limit finish naturally; nobody is cut off.
  • The table lists each agent with their status ("On a call", or their Amazon Connect status), when they signed in and when they were last seen.

Force logout frees a seat now, for example when someone left their softphone open and went home. 1. Press Force logout on the agent's row. 2. Confirm: "Sign name out?" → Yes, sign out. If the agent is on a call you see "name is on a call. Signing them out ends it." and the button is End the call and sign out; you are also asked to confirm it is you. 3. The agent's softphone shows "An administrator ended your softphone session. Open the softphone again from the call bar."

Seats also free themselves. A closed softphone window gives up its seat after about 45 seconds and a silent idle one after about 3 minutes. A window that dropped during a call keeps it for up to 15 minutes, so the agent can come back to the call.

docs.title: 6. Licence
docs.text:
"What your licence allows. The licence text itself is never shown here."

The page shows Status (Valid, Expires soon, Expired, in grace period, Expired, No licence, Not valid), Customer, Plan, Seats (and how many are in use), Valid until (with days left) and, for paid licences, Grace period ends. Warnings appear if the server is running on the last good licence or its clock looks wrong.

To install a new licence: paste the licence text under Replace the licence, press Check the licence, read "This will change:", then Apply the new licence (you may be asked to confirm it is you). "The new licence is in use." confirms it. What the states mean and how to renew: licence guide.

docs.title: 7. Change history
docs.text: "Who changed what, newest first. It holds ids only, never personal details." It lists settings changes (old and new value), licence changes, force logouts, sign-ins and failed sign-ins, lockouts, and changes to administrators and their sign-in methods. Show older loads more. The server keeps this record for six years by default.

docs.title: 8. Administrators
docs.text:
"Who can sign in to this console. An administrator can change anything. A read-only person can look but not change."

Invite someone 1. Under "Invite someone", type the email address and name, choose Administrator or Read only, and press Create a setup code (you may be asked to confirm it is you). 2. The page shows "Give email this setup code now. It is shown only once." Pass it on by a separate channel (for example in person or by phone), then press I have passed it on. 3. They open the console, choose I have a setup code and follow section 1. Until then their row says "Not set up yet".

Change access: use the Role list on a row. Turn off stops a person signing in without deleting them (Turn on reverses it). Remove deletes the account after "Yes, remove". The only administrator cannot be removed, turned off or made read-only: "The only administrator. Invite another first." Keep at least two administrators.

docs.title: 9. My sign-in
docs.text:
• Authenticator app: Set up an authenticator app or Replace the authenticator app (scan, then Confirm the code).
  • Passkeys: Add a passkey on each device you use; Remove one you no longer have.
  • Recovery codes: shows how many are left. Make new recovery codes replaces all of them ("Older codes no longer work").

Changes here ask you to confirm it is you. You cannot remove your last way to sign in.

docs.title: 10. Agent mapping (on the server, not in the console)
docs.text: Which GoHighLevel users get a call panel is decided by the agent mapping file on the server, backend/config/agents.json. Each line links a GoHighLevel email address (lower case) to an Amazon Connect user name. Your server administrator edits it. Changes apply at the agent's next sign-in, with no restart. An agent missing from it sees "email is not linked to an Amazon Connect agent. Ask your administrator to add you." See the installation guide.

docs.title: 11. Locked out
docs.text: Situation Way back in Wrong code several times Wait 15 minutes, then sign in with your email address and a current code. Lost phone or passkey I lost my phone with a recovery code, then set up again on My sign-in. No recovery codes left Another administrator invites you again (new setup code), or removes and re-invites you. No administrator can sign in Your server administrator makes a new setup code on the server and restarts the service (operations runbook).

docs.title: 12. Logging out
docs.text: Log out at the bottom of the menu. The page says "You have been logged out" and "Your admin session has ended. Settings you saved stay in effect. Agents on calls are not affected."

docs.title: Licence guide
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

How your organisation receives, installs and renews the connector licence, and what the licence and its notices mean. The licence applies only when the platform is switched on.

docs.title: What a licence is
docs.text:
A licence is a short text file signed by OctaveBytes. It says: - your organisation's name; - the product it is for; - the GoHighLevel sub-account (location id) it is bound to: it does not work on another sub-account; - how many seats may be in use at the same time (one seat = one open softphone window); - from when and until when it is valid, and whether it is a trial; - the grace period after the end date (paid licences only).

Your connector checks the signature by itself with OctaveBytes' public keys (a file on your server). It never contacts OctaveBytes. The licence text contains no personal data and is never shown in the console or written to logs.

docs.title: Receiving a licence
docs.text:
OctaveBytes sends you: 1. the licence file (one line of text, a file ending in .key); 2. the public keys file licence-keys.json, the first time and whenever OctaveBytes changes its keys.

Before a licence can be issued, tell OctaveBytes your organisation's name and your GoHighLevel sub-account's location id (it is in the address bar when you are in the sub-account: .../v2/location/<location id>/...).

docs.title: Installing or replacing the licence
docs.text:
In the admin console (recommended) 1. Open Licence. 2. Open the licence file in a text editor, copy all of it, and paste it under Replace the licence. 3. Press Check the licence and read "This will change:" (customer, seats, dates). 4. Press Apply the new licence. Confirm it is you if asked. "The new licence is in use." confirms it.

On the server (your server administrator) 1. Replace the file backend/data/license.key with the new licence (as the service user, keeping its permissions). 2. The connector notices the change within about 30 seconds; no restart is needed.

The public keys file goes to backend/config/licence-keys.json. The connector reads it only when it starts: after replacing it, restart the connector at a time when no call is in progress. If you forget, the Licence page says "The licence was signed with a key this system does not know." for a licence whose key you did add.

After installing, agents who were refused can open the softphone again from the call panel.

docs.title: Renewing
docs.text:
OctaveBytes issues licences for a fixed period. Before the end date, ask OctaveBytes for a renewal and install the new file in the same way. A renewal can also change the number of seats. Installing the renewal replaces the old licence at once. Nobody is signed out.

If you install a licence with fewer seats than are in use, agents already signed in carry on. New softphone windows are refused until the number in use is below the new limit.

docs.title: States and what they mean
docs.text:
State on the Licence page Meaning What agents notice Valid The licence is in force. Nothing. Expires soon The end date is within 30 days (3 days for a trial). A notice in the call panel: "The licence ends in N days. Ask your administrator to renew it." Expired, in grace period A paid licence has passed its end date and is in its grace period (normally 7 days; your licence says). "The licence has expired. Calls keep working for now. Ask your administrator to install a new licence." Expired Past the end date and any grace period. Trials have no grace period. Softphones already open keep working and calls are not cut. New softphone windows are refused: "… The softphone cannot start until it is fixed." No licence No licence file is installed. New softphone windows are refused. Not valid The file cannot be used (see the message on the page). New softphone windows are refused.

The page also shows these warnings when they apply: - "The licence shown is the last good one. The stored licence cannot be used right now." The file on the server was damaged or replaced by an unusable one; the connector keeps using the last good licence until it ends. Install a correct file. - "This computer's clock is earlier than a time already seen. Check the date and time." The server clock moved backwards. The connector judges the licence by the later of the clock and the latest time it has seen, so turning the clock back does not extend a licence. Fix the server's time setting.

docs.title: Messages when a licence is refused
docs.text: Message Cause Fix This is not a licence. The pasted text is not a licence file. Paste the whole file content, one line. The licence is damaged. / The licence could not be read. The text was changed or cut. Copy it again from the original file. The licence signature is not valid. The text was altered after signing. Ask OctaveBytes for the file again. The licence was signed with a key this system does not know. The public keys file does not contain the key that signed it, or the connector was not restarted after the keys file changed. Install the latest licence-keys.json from OctaveBytes and restart the connector. The licence is for a different account or system. It is bound to another GoHighLevel sub-account. Check the location id you gave OctaveBytes, and the one the server is set up for. The licence is for a different product. It was issued for another OctaveBytes product. Ask OctaveBytes for the right licence. The licence is not valid yet. Its start date is in the future. Wait, or check the server clock. This licence is from a newer version than this system understands. The connector needs an upgrade. Upgrade the connector (upgrade guide).

docs.title: Trials
docs.text: OctaveBytes can issue a trial licence. A trial has a fixed end date, shows "(trial)" on the Licence page, warns 3 days before the end, and has no grace period: on its end date new softphone windows are refused.

docs.title: Questions
docs.text: Licences, renewals and seat changes: support@octavebytes.com. Never send your server's files other than the licence itself.

docs.title: Settings reference
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

Every setting an administrator can change in the admin console, grouped as the console groups them (Settings in the menu). Settings exist only when the platform is switched on. Each one is enforced on the server, not only hidden on screen: an agent cannot get round a switched-off feature by changing their browser.

How changes reach agents: a saved change is sent to every open call panel at once. A call already in progress keeps the settings it started with; the change applies from the next call. Nothing changes until Save changes is pressed. How to use the console: admin guide.

The Key is the setting's permanent name. It appears in the change history and never changes once released.

docs.title: Calling
docs.text: Setting Key Default What it does Enforced Agents can place calls connect.outbound On Agents can dial from the call panel and use click-to-call. When off, the call panel hides the dial box and the server refuses any dial request. server refuses the DIAL request Agent chooses the queue connect.queueSelect On Agents can pick which outbound queue a call goes out on. When off, outbound calls use the agent's standard outbound queue. Has no effect while "Agents can place calls" is off. server drops a queue chosen by the agent Open the contact when a call comes in connect.screenPop On When a call rings, the matching contact opens in GoHighLevel. When off, the contact is not looked up or opened when a call rings. server contact lookup Hold and resumeControls during a call connect.hold On The Hold and Resume buttons during a call. When off, the server refuses both hold and resume. server refuses the HOLD request Keypad (send digits)Controls during a call connect.keypad On The Keypad button during a call, for sending digits (for example to an automated menu). server refuses the DTMF request MuteControls during a call connect.mute On The Mute button during a call. server refuses the MUTE request TransferControls during a call connect.transfer Off Call transfer. Not available in this release; the switch is shown as Planned and cannot be turned on. Planned. Not enforced (not available in this release) Record missed calls crm.missedTask On A call nobody answered still leaves a note and a call entry on the contact. When off, missed calls leave nothing in GoHighLevel. server call-record writer

docs.title: Wrap-up
docs.text: Setting Key Default What it does Enforced Wrap-up after calls connect.wrapEnabled On After a call the agent gets a wrap-up step (disposition and note) before the call is finished. When off, the call is logged straight away. server checks the wrap-up; server call-record writer A disposition is required connect.dispReq Off The agent must choose a disposition before finishing wrap-up. The server refuses to finish the call without one. Has no effect while "Wrap-up after calls" is off. server checks the wrap-up; server refuses the COMPLETE request Agents can add a note connect.notesShow On The notes box in wrap-up. Has no effect while "Wrap-up after calls" is off. server checks the wrap-up A note is required connect.notesReq Off The agent must type a note before finishing wrap-up. Has no effect while "Agents can add a note" is off. server checks the wrap-up Dispositions for inbound callsDispositions connect.dispIn Interested, Callback requested, Not interested, No answer, Wrong number, Other The dispositions offered after an inbound call (up to 30 entries, each up to 40 characters). The server refuses a value that is not in the list. server checks the wrap-up Dispositions for outbound callsDispositions connect.dispOut Interested, Callback requested, Not interested, No answer, Wrong number, Other The dispositions offered after an outbound call (same limits as the inbound list). server checks the wrap-up

docs.title: Conversation logging
docs.text: Setting Key Default What it does Enforced Create the call entry in GoHighLevel crm.logCall On Creates the native "Call completed" entry in the contact's conversation in GoHighLevel. server call-record writer Attach the recording to the call entry crm.pushRecording On Adds the recording player to the "Call completed" entry. The recording plays only for someone signed in to Amazon Connect with permission to hear recordings. Has no effect while "Create the call entry in GoHighLevel" is off. Needs the GoHighLevel call entry capability (a marketplace app with a conversation provider). server call-record writer Post the call transcript crm.pushTranscript On Posts the call transcript as one internal comment on the contact after the call. Independent of the live transcript switch. server AI summary job Write a note on the contact crm.noteOn On Writes a note on the contact with the call details after each call. server call-record writer Include the AI summary in the note crm.noteSummary On Adds the AI call summary to that note. Has no effect while "Write a note on the contact" is off. server call-record writer; server AI summary job Include the recording link in the note crm.noteRecUrl On Adds the Amazon Connect recording link to that note. Has no effect while "Write a note on the contact" is off. server call-record writer Include the disposition in the note crm.noteDisp On Adds the disposition to that note. The agent's own wrap-up note is always included. Has no effect while "Write a note on the contact" is off. server call-record writer

docs.title: AI assist
docs.text: Setting Key Default What it does Enforced Live suggestions (Amazon Q) connect.liveAssist On Amazon Q suggestions and the Ask Q box on the Assist tab during calls. When off, the Assist tab is hidden. server stops the live feed Live transcript connect.liveTranscript On The live transcript and caller sentiment on the Transcript tab during calls. When off, the Transcript tab is hidden. server stops the live feed AI call summary connect.aiSummary On Requests an AI call summary from Amazon Connect after each answered call and saves it to the contact. When off, the Summary tab is hidden. server AI summary job Suggest a disposition connect.autoDisp Off Suggesting a disposition with AI. Not available in this release; shown as Planned and cannot be turned on. Planned. Not enforced (not available in this release)

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text:
Setting Key Default What it does Enforced Connector switched on platform.enabled On The master switch. When off, every call panel disappears within about a minute, GoHighLevel's own dialler works again, and no new softphone sign-in is accepted. Calls already in progress finish and are still logged. server sign-in and status API Starting view of the call panel platform.panelMode full How the call panel first appears: full (calls, assist, transcript and summary tabs) or compact (calls only). Each agent can still switch, and their own choice is remembered in their browser. server sends it as the call panel's starting value Refresh the contact page after a call is saved platform.autoRefresh On After a call is saved, the contact page refreshes by itself so the new note shows, but only when it is safe (no call in progress, nothing being typed). Each agent can turn this off in the panel. server sends it as the call panel's starting value Create a contact for unknown callers crm.unknownCaller On When a number has no contact, one is created when the call rings or is dialled, named "Unknown caller" with the number. Withheld numbers are never created. server contact creation

29 settings in total.

docs.title: Installation guide
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

For the server administrator who installs the connector for one organisation and one GoHighLevel sub-account. Read requirements first. Every value below is an example: cti.example.com stands for your connector's address.

Read the output of the first-time setup script (server-setup.sh) as it runs, and be ready to adjust the port and certificate steps to your server.

Never paste secrets (tokens, keys, .env content, setup codes) into email, chat or tickets.

docs.title: 1. Prepare
docs.text: Item Example Connector address https://cti.example.com (a DNS A record pointing at the server) Server Ubuntu, Node.js 22, nginx and certbot installed, a free local port (default 4320) From GoHighLevel the sub-account location id and a Private Integration token created inside the sub-account From Amazon Connect the instance address (for example https://yourcompany.my.connect.aws), the instance id, the AWS region, the Amazon Q assistant id, and an IAM role for the server (or an access key) From OctaveBytes the release package (.tar.gz and its .sha256), the licence file, the public keys file licence-keys.json, and the Marketplace app values (app id, shared secret, client id, client secret, conversation provider id). Tell OctaveBytes your connector address first, so it can be added to the app. People the first console administrator's email address and name

docs.title: 2. Get the release package
docs.text:
OctaveBytes provides the package. To build it yourself from the source repository (Node.js 22):

npm ci
npm run verify
./deploy/package.sh /tmp/ob-ghl-connector.tar.gz

package.sh builds and checks the platform packages, includes them in the package, refuses to build if a secret file slipped in, and writes /tmp/ob-ghl-connector.tar.gz.sha256 next to the package with the version and commit it contains. The .sha256 file must travel with the package: the update script will not install without it.

docs.title: 3. Set up the server
docs.text:
Copy the package, its .sha256 file and the deploy/ folder to the server, then as root from that deploy/ folder:

./server-setup.sh cti.example.com /tmp/ob-ghl-connector.tar.gz 4320

The script only adds things: a service user obghl, the folder /opt/ob-ghl-connector, the systemd service ob-ghl-connector, an nginx site for your domain only, and a Let's Encrypt certificate for it. It backs up /etc/nginx first, checks that the domain points at this server and that the port is free, and prints the commands to undo it. It does not start the service while required values in .env are empty.

nginx. The site proxies everything to 127.0.0.1:<port>, allows WebSocket upgrades, keeps connections open for up to an hour, and limits request bodies to 64 KB (template: deploy/nginx-site.conf.template). Keep these lines if you edit it. To serve HTTPS on a port other than 443, add a listen <port> ssl server block with the same location / content and open the port in your firewall.

docs.title: 4. Fill in the environment file
docs.text:
Edit /opt/ob-ghl-connector/backend/.env (template: deploy/env.production.example). It is readable only by root and the service user. Keep it so. Changes need a restart.

Hosting

Variable Meaning TLS off: nginx handles HTTPS and the connector speaks plain HTTP on the local port. HOST 127.0.0.1: listen on the local address only. With this value the connector trusts nginx's forwarded client address. PORT The local port, the same as in the nginx site (default 4320). BACKEND_ORIGIN The public address agents use, with https:// and no trailing slash, for example https://cti.example.com. Used for the GoHighLevel app redirect, the allowed-address list, and passkeys. ALLOWED_ORIGINS Extra addresses agents open GoHighLevel from, comma-separated, for example your agency's white-label domain. *.gohighlevel.com is always allowed. Set it even if you use only app.gohighlevel.com, to replace the built-in default.

GoHighLevel

Variable Meaning GHL_LOCATION_ID The sub-account's location id. The licence is bound to it. GHL_PRIVATE_TOKEN The Private Integration token from inside the sub-account. Secret. GHL_APP_ID, GHL_APP_SHARED_SECRET The OctaveBytes Marketplace app's id and shared secret (from OctaveBytes); used to recognise the signed-in GoHighLevel user. The shared secret is secret. GHL_CLIENT_ID, GHL_CLIENT_SECRET The app's OAuth client (from OctaveBytes); used when the app is installed on the sub-account. The client secret is secret. GHL_PROVIDER_ID The app's conversation provider id (from OctaveBytes). Needed for the "Call completed" entry and the recording player. GHL_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY Optional. GoHighLevel's public key for checking webhook signatures. Without it every webhook is refused (nothing in this release uses webhooks yet).

Amazon Connect and AWS

Variable Meaning CONNECT_URL Your Amazon Connect instance address, for example https://yourcompany.my.connect.aws. CONNECT_INSTANCE_ID Your Amazon Connect instance id. Set it: the built-in value belongs to the OctaveBytes test instance. Q_ASSISTANT_ID Your Amazon Q in Connect assistant id. Set it for the same reason. AWS_REGION The region of your instance, for example us-east-1. AWS_AUTH role (recommended): use the server's IAM role, so no AWS key is stored. Leave the two key variables empty then. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Only if you do not use a role. Secret; rotate regularly.

The role or key needs the permissions in deploy/iam-policy.json (read contact details and Contact Lens results, use the Amazon Q assistant and its encryption key). deploy/iam-trust-policy.json lets an EC2 instance use the role.

Security

Variable Meaning SESSION_SECRET A long random value that signs agent tokens. Secret. Changing it signs every agent out. ADMIN_TOKEN 16 or more random characters; enables the detailed health check for operators. Secret. ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE can point at a file holding it instead. SESSION_MAX_HOURS How long a softphone session lasts before it must be reopened. Default 12. BAR_STALE_MIN Minutes after which a call panel whose GoHighLevel sign-in has stopped is disconnected (never during a call). Default 35. CSP_MODE enforce turns the content security policy on; default is report-only. Test with your softphone before enforcing.

Privacy and retention (see data and retention)

Variable Meaning RETENTION_DAYS Delete stored transcripts, summary jobs, call history, Amazon Q feedback and finished-call ledger entries older than this many days. Unset or 0 keeps everything. AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS Days to keep the audit log. Default 2190 (six years). AUDIT_DIR Where the audit log is written. Default backend/data/audit. PERSIST_TRANSCRIPT off keeps the live transcript in memory only. GHL_AI_TEXT off writes nothing produced by AI to GoHighLevel.

Alerts

Variable Meaning ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL Optional address that receives a short alert message (Slack-compatible; no personal data). ALERT_COOLDOWN_MIN Minimum minutes between two alerts of the same kind. Default 15.

Platform (licence, seats, admin console)

Variable Meaning PLATFORM on switches the platform on. Set by the platform install script (step 7). PLATFORM_LICENCE Leave unset (licence enforced). ADMIN_RP_ID The domain passkeys are tied to. Default: the host of BACKEND_ORIGIN. Changing the address later means administrators add their passkeys again. ADMIN_SECRET Optional, 32+ characters; signs console sessions. If unset, a random one is kept in backend/data/admin-secret.key.

Other: DEFAULT_COUNTRY (two letters, default US) is the country assumed for numbers typed without a country code. TRANSCRIPT, ASSIST and AUTO_CREATE_UNKNOWN (off) switch features off when the platform is off. With the platform on, use the console instead. DATA_DIR, CONFIG_DIR and ENV_FILE move the data folder, the configuration folder and the environment file. Leave DEV_MODE, DEBUG_PANEL, HOLD_MS, RETRY_BASE_MS, RECONCILE_MS and GHL_BASE unset: they are for development and tests.

docs.title: 5. Connect Amazon Connect and GoHighLevel
docs.text:
Do these in order.

  1. Amazon Connect approved origin. AWS console → Amazon Connect → your instance → Application integration → Approved origins → add https://cti.example.com (with the port if it is not 443). Without it the softphone window cannot start.
  2. Amazon Connect features. Make sure your contact flows enable call recording, Contact Lens real-time analytics and post-call summary, and create an Amazon Q session. These are standard Amazon Connect settings; your Amazon Connect administrator owns them.
  3. GoHighLevel Marketplace app. OctaveBytes adds https://cti.example.com/oauth/callback to its app's redirect URLs (tell OctaveBytes your address). Your agency administrator then installs the OctaveBytes app on the sub-account from the install link OctaveBytes sends. The install ends on a page that says "Connected to GoHighLevel. You can close this tab." The server keeps the app's token in backend/data/oauth.json. Only one server may use this token: GoHighLevel replaces it on every refresh.
  4. GoHighLevel Custom JS. In the agency: Settings → Company → White Label → Custom JS. Copy the current content somewhere safe first. Add:
<script src="https://cti.example.com/loader.js" async></script>

The editor sometimes duplicates the closing </script>. Check the end of the line. Save, and confirm the third-party scripts warning (Proceed). Agents reload GoHighLevel.

docs.title: 6. Link agents
docs.text:
Edit /opt/ob-ghl-connector/backend/config/agents.json (as root; keep it readable by the service user). One line per agent, GoHighLevel email address in lower case to Amazon Connect user name:

{
  "_comment": "GHL user email (lowercase) -> Amazon Connect username.",
  "agent.one@example.com": "agent.one",
  "agent.two@example.com": "agent.two"
}

The file is read on every sign-in, so no restart is needed. Changes are noted in the audit log (without the content).

docs.title: 7. Start the connector
docs.text:
systemctl start ob-ghl-connector
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4320/health
curl -s https://cti.example.com/health

Both health checks answer {"ok":true,...}. Logs: journalctl -u ob-ghl-connector -n 50.

docs.title: 8. Switch the platform on and create the first administrator
docs.text:
The platform adds the licence, seats, settings and the admin console. Without it the connector works with all features on and no seat limit.

  1. Put the public keys file from OctaveBytes at /opt/ob-ghl-connector/backend/config/licence-keys.json (owner root, group obghl, mode 640).
  2. Put the licence file at /opt/ob-ghl-connector/backend/data/license.key (owned by obghl). Or install it later on the console's Licence page.
  3. Read deploy/install-platform.sh, then run it as root with the address agents use and the first administrator:
./install-platform.sh https://cti.example.com admin@example.com "Admin Name"

It asks before changing anything, keeps a copy of .env, sets PLATFORM=on, BACKEND_ORIGIN and AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS=2190, prints a one-time setup code (24 hours, single use), restarts the service and checks it answers. 4. Give the setup code to the first administrator by a separate channel. They open https://cti.example.com/admin/, choose I have a setup code, set up an authenticator app and, where offered, a passkey, and save their recovery codes (admin guide). 5. Check the log line: journalctl -u ob-ghl-connector -n 20 | grep platform shows [platform] on: licence valid for <customer>, N seat(s); settings rev …; passkeys on. "passkeys off (authenticator app only)" means the address has no domain name or is not HTTPS.

To make another setup code later (for example when every administrator is locked out), see the operations runbook.

docs.title: 9. Check it works
docs.text:
# Check Expected 1 https://cti.example.com/health {"ok":true,...} with a valid certificate 2 https://cti.example.com/loader.js the loader script 3 GoHighLevel in a fresh Chrome profile, as a mapped agent the call panel appears 4 Open softphone, sign in to Amazon Connect the panel shows the agent's status 5 A test call in and out ring, accept, hold, mute, hang up, wrap-up, "Logged to GHL", note and call entry on the contact 6 After an answered call AI summary and transcript comment on the contact a few seconds later 7 /admin/ sign-in works; Agents shows the seat; Licence shows Valid 8 curl -I https://cti.example.com/engine.html referrer-policy: strict-origin and no camera=() in permissions-policy (see troubleshooting)

Use test contacts and test calls only. No real patient data during installation.

docs.title: 10. Undo the installation
docs.text:
1. GoHighLevel Custom JS: remove the loader.js line (agents reload). This alone removes the connector from GoHighLevel.
  2. systemctl disable --now ob-ghl-connector
  3. rm /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/ob-ghl-connector && nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx
  4. Remove the approved origin in Amazon Connect.

Next: upgrade and rollback · operations runbook.

docs.title: Operations runbook
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

Day-to-day running of the connector: checks, logs, backups and the usual incidents. Commands run on the server as root unless stated. Paths are under /opt/ob-ghl-connector/backend/. Never copy the contents of .env, data/ or config/ into email, chat or tickets.

docs.title: Where things are
docs.text: Path What it is .env Environment settings and secrets (read at start) config/agents.json Agent mapping (read on every sign-in) config/licence-keys.json OctaveBytes public keys (read only at start) config/settings.json Settings used when the platform is off data/oauth.json GoHighLevel app token (only one server may use it) data/license.key The licence (re-read within about 30 seconds of a change) data/settings.json Console settings and their last 20 versions data/admins.json, data/admin-secret.key Administrator accounts; the key that signs console sessions data/seats.json Who holds a seat data/pending.json, data/ledger.json Calls still being written; recently finished calls (so nothing is written twice) data/calls.jsonl Call history (feeds agents' recent calls) data/transcripts/, data/summaries/ Stored transcripts and AI summary jobs data/audit/ Audit log, one file per day /opt/ob-ghl-connector/VERSION, RELEASES.log Installed version; update history /root/backups/ Backups made by each update

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text:
Check Command Healthy Public curl -s https://cti.example.com/health "ok":true, "ghlToken" present, transcript, summary and assist status not in error Switched on curl -s https://cti.example.com/v2/status {"ok":true,"enabled":true} Detail (operators) curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin token>" http://127.0.0.1:4320/health?detail=1 queue depth 0 or falling, no dead items, rooms listed, alert counters low Service systemctl status ob-ghl-connector active (running) Certificate systemctl list-timers \| grep certbot a renewal timer is scheduled Console /admin/ → Agents and Licence seats as expected; licence Valid

The detailed check needs ADMIN_TOKEN (16+ characters) in .env. It is rate-limited and every use is audited.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
• Service log: journalctl -u ob-ghl-connector -f (live) or -n 100 --no-pager. Phone numbers show only the last four digits; no transcript text.
  • Start-up lines tell you the address, the GoHighLevel token state and, with the platform on, [platform] on: licence <state> …, N seat(s); settings rev N; passkeys on|off.
  • ALERT lines mark repeated failures (refused sign-ins, rate limits, AWS credential errors, a call that could not be written, server exceptions). If ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL is set they are also sent there.
  • HOOK SELF-TEST: missing … means GoHighLevel changed a page element the call panel relies on (for example the phone icon). Report it to support@octavebytes.com; agents can still dial from the panel.
  • Audit log: data/audit/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl, ids only. Forward it to your log store (a CloudWatch agent configuration is in deploy/cloudwatch-agent.json).

docs.title: Backups
docs.text: Back up data/ and config/ (and .env in a secrets store) every night, for example with disk snapshots. The program itself can always be reinstalled from the release package. Use an encrypted disk and encrypted backups: data/ holds call records, transcripts and the GoHighLevel token.

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
1. systemctl stop ob-ghl-connector. Move the damaged data/ aside; do not delete it.
  2. Restore data/ and config/ from your backup. Order of importance: oauth.json, license.key, settings.json, admins.json, admin-secret.key, seats.json, pending.json and ledger.json, calls.jsonl.
  3. If oauth.json from the backup is older than the last token refresh, GoHighLevel will refuse it: reinstall the Marketplace app on the sub-account (installation guide, step 5.3).
  4. systemctl start ob-ghl-connector, then check /health and the first log lines.
  5. Seats come back with a two-minute grace, so returning softphones keep their seat; unfinished call records continue writing by themselves.

docs.title: Licence expiry
docs.text:
The Licence page and the call panel warn 30 days before the end (3 days for a trial). Ask OctaveBytes for a renewal and install it (licence guide). If the page still says the licence is not valid after installing: - the licence is for another location id than GHL_LOCATION_ID; - the signing key is missing from config/licence-keys.json, or the service was not restarted after that file changed; - the server clock is wrong.

Fix the cause, not the licence.

docs.title: A seat is stuck
docs.text:
Symptom: an agent is refused ("No softphone seat is free right now…") but nobody seems to be using the seats.

  1. Console → Agents: who holds a seat, their status and when they were last seen.
  2. Seats free themselves: a closed window after about 45 seconds, a silent idle window after about 3 minutes, a window that dropped during a call after up to 15 minutes.
  3. To free one now: Force logout on that row (admin guide).
  4. Last resort, if the Agents page itself is wrong: stop the service, delete data/seats.json, start the service. Every softphone reconnects and takes a seat again; nobody is signed out of GoHighLevel.

docs.title: Administrator locked out
docs.text:
1. If another administrator can sign in, they invite the person again from Administrators.
  2. Otherwise, on the server as the service user, make a new setup code, then restart (the code is read at start):
cd /opt/ob-ghl-connector/backend && sudo -u obghl node platform/invite.js admin@example.com "Admin Name"
systemctl restart ob-ghl-connector

The code is printed once, works once and expires after 24 hours. Restart when no call is in progress. The person opens /admin/, chooses I have a setup code and sets up again. Turn off the old account afterwards if it is not needed. Never edit data/admins.json by hand.

docs.title: Switch the connector off for everyone
docs.text:
• Platform on: console → Settings → Advanced → switch off Connector switched on → Save changes.
  • Platform off: set {"enabled": false} in config/settings.json (no restart).

Every call panel disappears within about a minute and GoHighLevel's own dialler works again. Calls in progress finish in the softphone window and are logged. Switch on again the same way. Panels come back without a reload.

Emergency without the server: remove the loader.js line from GoHighLevel Custom JS and ask agents to reload.

docs.title: Switch the platform off
docs.text:
Removes the licence, seats and console, and returns to the settings in config/settings.json and the environment.

  1. Remove the PLATFORM=on line from .env (the install script left a copy of the previous .env beside it).
  2. systemctl restart ob-ghl-connector when no call is in progress.

Nothing is deleted. Switching on again picks up the saved console settings and accounts. Settings saved in the console are not copied into config/settings.json.

docs.title: Secrets and keys
docs.text: Item When to change How SESSION_SECRET If exposed New random value, restart when no call is in progress. Every agent is signed out of the connector; agents reload GoHighLevel and open the softphone again. ADMIN_TOKEN If exposed, or regularly New random value (16+ characters), restart. AWS access key Regularly; better replaced by an IAM role (AWS_AUTH=role) Rotate in AWS, update .env, restart, then test a call and an AI summary. GoHighLevel Private Integration token If exposed Create a new one in the sub-account, update .env, restart. Public keys file When OctaveBytes sends a new one Replace config/licence-keys.json, restart when no call is in progress.

docs.title: Certificates
docs.text: certbot renews the certificate automatically and reloads nginx. Check the timer once after installation and after server upgrades.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text: See upgrade and rollback. Re-run npm audit on the source before each release (OctaveBytes does this for its packages).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

Symptom, cause and fix for the problems seen so far. Agent-facing messages are listed in the agent guide. Start with the service log: journalctl -u ob-ghl-connector -n 100 --no-pager.

docs.title: The softphone window keeps going back to sign-in or says "refused to connect"
docs.text: Symptom: the softphone window loops between a "refused to connect" frame and the Amazon Connect sign-in screen, or shows "Camera is not accessible". Cause: the page that holds the Amazon Connect softphone must send Referrer-Policy: strict-origin. With no-referrer, Amazon Connect cannot see which site is asking and refuses to be shown (frame-ancestors 'self'). A Permissions-Policy that blocks the camera (camera=()) makes the softphone show "Camera is not accessible". Release v2.0.0 sends the right headers; this happens when an older release is still installed, or when nginx adds its own security headers. Fix: 1. curl -sI https://cti.example.com/engine.html must show referrer-policy: strict-origin and must not show camera=(). 2. Check the installed release: cat /opt/ob-ghl-connector/VERSION. 3. Remove any add_header Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy lines from the nginx site for this connector, reload nginx. 4. Check the connector's address is in Amazon Connect Approved origins (with the port if not 443).

docs.title: The softphone window is blank
docs.text: Cause: the service user cannot read the program files, usually after files were unpacked by hand. Fix: chown -R root:obghl /opt/ob-ghl-connector, chmod -R u=rwX,g=rX,o= /opt/ob-ghl-connector, chown -R obghl:obghl /opt/ob-ghl-connector/backend/data, restart. The log shows EACCES errors in this case.

docs.title: "Allow pop-ups for this site, then try again."
docs.text: Fix: in Chrome, allow pop-ups for the GoHighLevel address, then click Open softphone again.

docs.title: "This Amazon Connect user is not the agent linked to your GoHighLevel account (…)"
docs.text: Cause: the agent signed in to Amazon Connect as another user, or the agent mapping points at the wrong Amazon Connect user name. Fix: sign out of Amazon Connect in the softphone window and sign in as the right user. Or correct config/agents.json.

docs.title: "The softphone is already open in another window or computer. Close this one."
docs.text: Cause: one softphone per agent. Fix: use the open one, or close it and open again.

docs.title: "No softphone seat is free right now…"
docs.text: Cause: all seats in use, or a seat held by a window that was left open. Fix: operations runbook: a seat is stuck.

docs.title: The call panel does not appear
docs.text: Cause Fix The Custom JS line is missing or broken GoHighLevel agency → Settings → Company → White Label → Custom JS: check the loader.js line and that </script> is not duplicated. The connector is switched off curl https://cti.example.com/v2/status shows "enabled":false. Switch it on (runbook). The agent opens GoHighLevel from an address the connector does not accept Add the agency's white-label address to ALLOWED_ORIGINS and restart. The log shows ws refused: Forbidden origin. The agent is not mapped The panel says "… is not linked to an Amazon Connect agent". Add them to config/agents.json. "This connector is not enabled for this sub-account." The agent is in another sub-account than GHL_LOCATION_ID.

docs.title: The panel stays on "Reconnecting…"
docs.text: Cause: the browser cannot keep the WebSocket connection to /relay. Fix: check the service is running. Check nginx passes WebSocket upgrades and long timeouts (installation guide, step 3). Check company proxies allow WebSocket.

docs.title: Click-to-call opens GoHighLevel's own dialler
docs.text: Cause: the softphone is not open ("Softphone off"), or GoHighLevel changed its page. Fix: open the softphone. If it persists, look for HOOK SELF-TEST: missing in the log and tell support@octavebytes.com. Agents can still dial from the panel.

docs.title: A call is missing in GoHighLevel
docs.text:
1. The detailed health check (/health?detail=1) lists calls still being written with their attempts and last error. The server retries for about three hours.
  2. A call whose softphone window vanished (browser closed, laptop died) is closed and written after about 5 minutes (call.engine_lost in the audit log).
  3. Check the settings: Record missed calls, Create the call entry in GoHighLevel, Write a note on the contact.
  4. ghlToken in /health should not report an error; if the app token was lost, reinstall the Marketplace app.

docs.title: No "Call completed" entry or no recording player
docs.text: Cause: the Marketplace app is not installed (no data/oauth.json) or GHL_PROVIDER_ID is empty. Or Attach the recording to the call entry is off. The note is still written.

docs.title: The recording player shows 0:00
docs.text: Cause: the viewer is not signed in to Amazon Connect with permission to hear recordings (the connector does not make recordings public). Or the call entry was created before Amazon Connect finished saving the recording. The connector waits up to 25 seconds for the recording when it has AWS access keys. With AWS_AUTH=role it does not wait in this release. Fix: sign in to Amazon Connect in the same browser and reload.

docs.title: No AI summary or transcript
docs.text: Message or state Cause Fix "No AI summary: the conversation was too short to summarise." Very short call Nothing to fix. "Live transcription is unavailable: the server cannot sign in to AWS." / "Q is unavailable: the server cannot sign in to AWS." AWS role or key missing or wrong Check AWS_AUTH or the keys, the IAM permissions, AWS_REGION. The log shows credentials rejected and an alert. Transcript or summary never appears Contact Lens not enabled in the contact flow, or CONNECT_INSTANCE_ID not set to your instance Enable Contact Lens real-time and post-call summary; set CONNECT_INSTANCE_ID and restart. Amazon Q never suggests No Amazon Q session in the contact flow, or Q_ASSISTANT_ID not set to your assistant Fix the flow; set Q_ASSISTANT_ID. The tab is missing Switched off in the console (AI assist page) Switch on and save.

docs.title: "Not logged yet, retrying: …"
docs.text: GoHighLevel refused or did not answer. The server keeps trying. If it continues for hours, check the GoHighLevel token and the detailed health check.

docs.title: "The licence was signed with a key this system does not know." after editing the keys file
docs.text: Cause: config/licence-keys.json is read only when the service starts. Fix: restart the connector at a time when no call is in progress. Check that the file is valid JSON (a list of entries with kid and publicKeyPem) and readable by the service user.

docs.title: Other licence messages
docs.text: See the licence guide.

docs.title: Sign-in fails with "Sign-in failed. Check the details and try again, or wait a few minutes."
docs.text:
Cause Fix Only the code was typed Type the email address as well as the code. A code alone is treated as an unknown account (the audit log shows admin.login_failed with admin unknown). Wrong entry in the authenticator app Each system has its own entry; pick the one for this console. Phone clock wrong Set the phone's time to automatic. Locked after 5 failures Wait 15 minutes. Lost phone I lost my phone with a recovery code. Nobody can sign in New setup code on the server (runbook).

A passkey needs neither the code nor the lock wait, but it needs the same domain the passkey was added on.

docs.title: No passkey option
docs.text: Cause: the console has no domain name (an IP address) or is not on HTTPS. The log says passkeys off (authenticator app only). Fix: use a domain name with HTTPS for BACKEND_ORIGIN, restart. Changing the domain later means passkeys must be added again.

docs.title: "The admin area is only available over https."
docs.text: Cause: the console was opened over plain HTTP, or nginx does not pass X-Forwarded-Proto. Fix: use the HTTPS address. Keep HOST=127.0.0.1 and the nginx header lines from the template.

docs.title: "This request did not come from the admin page."
docs.text: Cause: the change came from another address than the console's own (for example a different host name or port). Fix: open the console at exactly BACKEND_ORIGIN + /admin/.

docs.title: "Someone else changed the same setting. Review the new value and save again."
docs.text: Another administrator saved first. Choose Use theirs or Keep mine on each row and save again.

docs.title: Commands that fail on the wrong machine
docs.text: Server commands run on your own computer fail with "unknown user" or "no such file". Check the prompt shows the server before running them.

docs.title: Upgrade and rollback
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

How to install a new release, and how to go back.

docs.title: What an update keeps
docs.text:
The update replaces the program only. It never touches: - backend/.env (your settings and secrets), - backend/config/ (agent mapping, public keys file), - backend/data/ (GoHighLevel app token, licence, console settings, administrators, seats, call records, audit log).

Example configuration files in the package are refreshed beside your own.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
1. Read the release notes for the new version.
  2. Choose a quiet time. The restart drops every softphone connection for a few seconds; calls are not cut, but agents may see "Reconnecting…".
  3. Check no call is in progress and nothing is waiting to be written:
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin token>" "http://127.0.0.1:4320/health?detail=1"

Look for a queue depth of 0 and every room idle. (Type the token from .env without leaving it in your shell history, for example by reading it into a variable and unsetting it afterwards.)

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
1. Copy the new package and its .sha256 file, plus deploy/update.sh from the same release, to /tmp on the server.
  2. As root:
cd /tmp && bash ./update.sh /tmp/ob-ghl-connector.tar.gz

The script: - refuses to install if the checksum does not match the .sha256 file (or EXPECTED_SHA256 if you received the checksum separately), or if any file differs from the package's own file list; - shows the old and the new version; - backs up the current program to /root/backups/ob-ghl-connector-pre-<date-time>.tgz; - unpacks the new program, installs its dependencies, sets file owners and permissions, restarts the service and checks that it answers; - adds a line to /opt/ob-ghl-connector/RELEASES.log.

It ends with updated; app answers on 127.0.0.1:4320. On a machine where tar prints harmless LIBARCHIVE warnings, you can filter them: bash ./update.sh … 2>&1 | grep -v LIBARCHIVE. 3. Check:

cat /opt/ob-ghl-connector/VERSION
curl -s https://cti.example.com/v2/status
journalctl -u ob-ghl-connector -n 12 --no-pager

VERSION shows the new version and commit. The status answers {"ok":true,"enabled":true}. With the platform on, the log shows [platform] on: licence valid …. 4. Agents reload GoHighLevel and, if their softphone window closed, open it again from the call panel.

First confirm which release the server really runs (VERSION) before comparing behaviour between releases.

docs.title: Roll back
docs.text:
Preferred: reinstall the previous release package. Keep the previous package and its .sha256 file. Install it with update.sh exactly as above. This brings back the previous program together with its own platform packages and dependencies, and keeps .env, config/ and data/.

From the backup the update made. The backup in /root/backups/ holds the previous program but not its installed dependencies (node_modules folders are left out). Use it only when the previous package is not available, and reinstall the dependencies afterwards:

systemctl stop ob-ghl-connector
tar -xzf /root/backups/ob-ghl-connector-pre-<date-time>.tgz -C /opt/ob-ghl-connector --exclude='./backend/data' --exclude='./backend/.env' --exclude='./backend/config'
cd /opt/ob-ghl-connector/backend && npm ci --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund
chown -R root:obghl /opt/ob-ghl-connector && chmod -R u=rwX,g=rX,o= /opt/ob-ghl-connector
find /opt/ob-ghl-connector -type d ! -path "*/node_modules/*" -exec chmod 750 {} +
chown -R obghl:obghl /opt/ob-ghl-connector/backend/data
systemctl start ob-ghl-connector
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4320/health

The platform packages in /opt/ob-ghl-connector/node_modules/@octavebytes/ stay at the newer version with this method. Use the reinstall method above instead.

Whichever method you use: - Do not use tar --no-same-owner without fixing the owners afterwards: files owned only by root cannot be read by the service user, and the softphone window then stays blank. - Never restore backend/data/ from an old backup as part of a rollback: the GoHighLevel app token changes over time, and an old copy no longer works. - Rolling back to an earlier release keeps call records safe: files keep the older field names beside the new ones. Console settings and administrator accounts are ignored by a release without the platform and come back when you upgrade again.

docs.title: Switching the platform off instead
docs.text: If a problem is with the licence, seats or console only, you can switch the platform off without rolling back: see the operations runbook.

docs.title: Product overview
docs.text: Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
The GHL CTI Connector for Amazon Connect puts an Amazon Connect phone inside GoHighLevel. Agents answer and place calls without leaving the CRM. The caller's contact opens by itself, the call is written to the contact when it ends, and Amazon Connect's AI adds a live transcript, suggested answers and a call summary.

It is made by OctaveBytes and runs on a server your organisation controls. Your calls stay in your Amazon Connect instance and your contact records stay in your GoHighLevel account.

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text:
• Teams that sell or support customers from GoHighLevel and use, or plan to use, Amazon Connect for their phone lines.
  • Agents, who want one screen for calls and customer records.
  • Team leads and administrators, who decide what agents can do on a call and what is written to the CRM.
  • Organisations with privacy duties, who need call data to stay in their own accounts. See Security and privacy.

docs.title: The problem it solves
docs.text:
Without it, agents switch between the Amazon Connect softphone and GoHighLevel: they look the caller up by hand, copy numbers to dial, and type call notes afterwards. Notes get missed, the CRM shows no record of the call, and supervisors cannot see what was said.

With the connector: - the phone is part of GoHighLevel, on every page; - the right contact opens when a call rings, and a contact is created for a new number; - every call leaves a note and a "Call completed" entry with the recording on the contact, written once even if a network or server problem interrupts it; - the live transcript, Amazon Q suggestions and an AI call summary help the agent during and after the call; - administrators switch features on and off for everyone from one console, and the server enforces those choices.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph Agent's browser
    P["Call panel<br/>(inside GoHighLevel)"]
    S["Softphone window<br/>(Amazon Connect phone)"]
  end
  subgraph Your server
    C["Connector<br/>+ admin console"]
  end
  GHL[("GoHighLevel<br/>contacts, notes,<br/>call entries")]
  AC[("Amazon Connect<br/>calls, recordings,<br/>Contact Lens, Amazon Q")]
  P <-- "secure connection" --> C
  S <-- "secure connection" --> C
  S <-- "voice" --> AC
  C -- "look up and write<br/>contacts and call records" --> GHL
  C -- "read call status,<br/>transcript, summary,<br/>suggestions" --> AC
  A["Administrator"] -- "admin console" --> C
  1. GoHighLevel loads the call panel on every page for agents your administrator has linked to an Amazon Connect user.
  2. The agent opens the softphone window once from the panel and signs in to Amazon Connect there. The voice travels between this window and Amazon Connect; the connector never carries audio.
  3. The connector on your server passes call events between the panel and the softphone, looks the caller up in GoHighLevel, and after the call writes the note, the call entry and the AI summary to the contact.
  4. Administrators use the admin console on the same server to change settings, manage seats and install the licence.

It does not host your data at OctaveBytes. It does not contact OctaveBytes to check the licence. It does not replace Amazon Connect's own tools for supervisors and reporting.
