docs.title: Security and privacy
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

What the connector handles, where it keeps it and how access is controlled, as built in release v2.0.0. This is a description of the software. It is not a compliance statement, a contract or legal advice, and it does not replace your own risk assessment.

docs.title: Where it runs
docs.text: The connector runs on a server your organisation controls, ideally in your own AWS account next to your Amazon Connect instance. Calls and recordings stay in your Amazon Connect instance. Contact records stay in your GoHighLevel account. The connector software does not send data to OctaveBytes: no usage data, no logs, no licence checks. (Support access that you choose to give OctaveBytes is a separate arrangement; see below.)

docs.title: Data handled
docs.text:
Data Where it comes from Where it goes or is kept Voice The caller and the agent Between the agent's softphone window and Amazon Connect only. The connector never carries audio. Recordings Amazon Connect Stay in your Amazon Connect storage. GoHighLevel holds only a link; it plays only for someone signed in to Amazon Connect with permission to hear recordings. Phone number, direction, duration, queue, agent, times Amazon Connect, through the softphone window The connector's call records on your server, and the note and call entry in GoHighLevel. Contact details (name, owner, last interaction, open deals) GoHighLevel Shown in the call panel. The contact's name is kept with the call record on your server (it feeds the agent's recent calls list); the other details are held briefly in the server's memory only. Disposition and the agent's note The agent The connector's call records, then the GoHighLevel note. Live transcript and sentiment Contact Lens Shown in the call panel. Stored on your server unless transcripts are kept in memory only (see Retention). Posted to GoHighLevel as one internal comment if that setting is on. AI call summary Contact Lens Shown in the call panel; written to GoHighLevel (comment, note, two contact fields) if those settings are on. Amazon Q suggestions, Ask Q questions and answers Amazon Q Shown in the call panel. Helpful or not-helpful marks are stored on your server and sent to Amazon Q. Administrator accounts Your administrators Your server: name, email, role, the authenticator secret (encrypted), recovery codes (stored as hashes only), passkey public keys. Licence OctaveBytes One file on your server. It holds your organisation's name, the GoHighLevel location id, seats and dates. No personal data.

A switch on the server (GHL_AI_TEXT=off) stops everything produced by AI (transcript comment, summary in the note, summary fields) from being written to GoHighLevel. The note keeps the call details and the agent's own note. Administrators can also switch off each part of the record in the console (settings reference).

docs.title: What is kept out of logs
docs.text:
• Transcript text, summaries and Ask Q text are never written to the server log.
  • Phone numbers in the server log show only the last four digits; email addresses are masked; contact names are not logged. The call panel and softphone window do not print numbers to the browser console.
  • Tokens, setup codes, recovery codes, passphrases and the licence text are never logged or written to the audit log.
  • The audit log holds ids only. An automated test runs a full scenario and fails if the log or audit files contain an email address, a phone number, a token, a key, a code or licence text.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
What Default How to change Transcripts, AI summary jobs, call history, Amazon Q feedback, finished-call ledger on the server Kept until you delete them RETENTION_DAYS=N on the server deletes them after N days (checked at start and every six hours). Live transcript on disk Stored PERSIST_TRANSCRIPT=off keeps it in memory only and drops transcript text from the summary job once it ends. Audit log Six years (2,190 days) AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS. Data written to GoHighLevel Kept by GoHighLevel Deleted in GoHighLevel by you. Recordings, Contact Lens results Kept by Amazon Connect Your Amazon Connect and storage retention rules.

Details per file: Data and retention.

docs.title: Sign-in
docs.text:
Agents do not have a separate password for the connector. When an agent opens GoHighLevel, the call panel asks GoHighLevel who is signed in, and the server checks that this GoHighLevel user is on the agent mapping and belongs to the right sub-account. The agent then signs in to Amazon Connect in the softphone window with their Amazon Connect credentials. The server issues short-lived tokens (15 minutes, renewed every 10 minutes while GoHighLevel stays signed in). A softphone session ends after 12 hours and must be opened again. A call panel whose GoHighLevel sign-in has stopped is disconnected after 35 minutes, never during a call.

Administrators sign in to the admin console with a passkey or an authenticator app code. There are no passwords and no shared default account. - The first administrator, and every new one, starts with a one-time setup code (single use, 24 hours). - Five wrong attempts lock the account for 15 minutes. The message is the same for an unknown address and a wrong code, so the page does not reveal who has an account. - Sessions end after 30 minutes without activity and after 8 hours at most. - Sensitive actions (installing a licence, inviting, changing or removing administrators, changing sign-in methods, ending the session of an agent who is on a call) ask the administrator to confirm it is them again if their last check was more than 10 minutes ago. - Ten recovery codes, each usable once, are given at setup. - Roles: administrator (can change everything) and read-only. The last administrator cannot be removed, turned off or made read-only.

docs.title: Licence: offline by design
docs.text: The licence is a text file signed by OctaveBytes. Your server checks the signature with OctaveBytes' public keys, which are installed with the connector. Nothing is sent to OctaveBytes and the connector never asks OctaveBytes for permission. Because of this a licence cannot be withdrawn remotely; OctaveBytes issues licences for a fixed period and renews them. The private signing key is never on your server. See the licence guide.

docs.title: Audit trail
docs.text: The server writes an append-only audit log, one file per day, readable only by the service account. It records sign-ins and refused sign-ins, setting changes (which setting and by which administrator id), seat events, licence changes, softphone sessions opened and ended, call commands by type, calls logged, configuration file changes, rate limits hit and retention runs. The console's Change history page shows the administrator-facing part of it, with names resolved from ids.

docs.title: Transport and web security
docs.text:
• All traffic between browsers and the connector uses HTTPS behind nginx; the server sends HSTS.
  • The connector accepts requests only from GoHighLevel addresses, its own address and addresses you list. The admin console accepts changes only from its own page.
  • Agent tokens, softphone tokens and console sessions are separate and cannot be used in place of one another. The console sets no cookies.
  • Sign-in, setup and webhook addresses are rate-limited.
  • A content security policy is sent in report-only mode by default; it can be enforced with CSP_MODE=enforce after testing with your softphone.
  • Repeated failures (refused sign-ins, rate limits, AWS credential errors, a call that could not be written to GoHighLevel) raise alerts in the log and, optionally, to a webhook you choose.

docs.title: Health-care data (HIPAA)
docs.text:
The connector is designed to support a customer's HIPAA programme. It is not "HIPAA certified" (no such certification exists for a product), and compliance depends on your whole setup. Safeguards that exist in release v2.0.0: - deployed in your own environment, with nothing sent to OctaveBytes; - authentication of every agent and administrator, isolation between agents, automatic log-off; - audit controls with no personal data in the audit log, kept six years by default; - minimum-necessary switches for what is written to GoHighLevel, and retention controls on the server; - a least-privilege AWS policy and an instance-role mode so no AWS key is stored on the server; - a checked update package (checksum verified before installing).

Your responsibilities include: a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with AWS and with GoHighLevel where required, encryption of the server disk and recording storage, backups, operating-system patching, access to the server, agent device security, your risk analysis and policies.

A BAA with OctaveBytes. OctaveBytes does not offer the connector as a hosted service: it is installed and runs in your environment, the data stays in your accounts and remains yours, and OctaveBytes does not receive or store it. For that reason a BAA with OctaveBytes is not normally required for the software itself. Whether one is needed depends on your own assessment, for example if OctaveBytes staff will have access to your systems or data for installation or support. OctaveBytes is open to signing a BAA where a customer needs one. Ask support@octavebytes.com.

docs.title: Frequently asked questions
docs.text: Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

docs.title: About the product
docs.text:
What is the GHL CTI Connector for Amazon Connect? A phone inside GoHighLevel for teams that use Amazon Connect. Agents answer and place calls from a panel on every GoHighLevel page, the caller's contact opens by itself, and each call is written to the contact. See the product overview.

Do we need Amazon Connect already? Yes. The connector uses your Amazon Connect instance for the calls, recordings, transcript, summary and Amazon Q. It does not provide phone numbers or call minutes.

Which GoHighLevel plan do we need? An agency account that can add Custom JS, a sub-account for your agents, a Private Integration token in that sub-account, and the OctaveBytes Marketplace app installed on it. See requirements.

Does it work with other CRMs? This release works with GoHighLevel only.

Is there a trial? OctaveBytes can arrange a trial licence. Ask support@octavebytes.com.

docs.title: Data and privacy
docs.text:
Where is our data stored? On your own server, in your Amazon Connect instance and in your GoHighLevel account. The connector software does not send data to OctaveBytes. See security and privacy.

Can OctaveBytes see our calls? Not through the product: the connector software does not send data to OctaveBytes, and the licence is checked offline. If you give OctaveBytes access to your systems for support, that is a separate arrangement that you control.

Are recordings public? No. GoHighLevel stores only a link. It plays only for someone signed in to Amazon Connect with permission to hear recordings.

Is it HIPAA compliant? No product can be "HIPAA certified". The connector is designed to support your HIPAA programme, with safeguards described in security and privacy. Compliance depends on your whole setup, including your agreements with AWS and GoHighLevel.

Will OctaveBytes sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA)? The connector runs in your environment and OctaveBytes does not receive or store your data, so a BAA with OctaveBytes is not normally required for the software itself. If your assessment says you need one, for example because OctaveBytes will help with installation or support on your systems, OctaveBytes is open to signing it. Ask support@octavebytes.com.

Can we stop AI text being written to GoHighLevel? Yes. Administrators can switch off the transcript comment, the AI summary and each part of the note in the console. A server setting (GHL_AI_TEXT=off) stops all AI text going to GoHighLevel.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
Do agents need another password? No. They are recognised through GoHighLevel and sign in to Amazon Connect in the softphone window, as they would anyway.

Why is the softphone a separate window? GoHighLevel reloads parts of its pages as agents move around. Keeping the phone in its own window means a page change never drops a call.

What happens if the internet drops during a call? The call is carried by Amazon Connect and usually continues. The panel shows "Reconnecting…" and catches up when the connection returns. The agent keeps their seat for up to 15 minutes. The call is written to the contact once.

Can an agent use two computers? One softphone window per agent at a time. A second window, on the same or another computer, is refused with "The softphone is already open in another window or computer. Close this one." Close the first window before opening the softphone elsewhere.

docs.title: Seats and licence
docs.text:
What is a seat? One open softphone window, whatever the agent's status, including Offline. If you have 10 seats, 10 agents can have the softphone open at once. You can have more agents than seats.

What happens when all seats are in use? The next agent who opens the softphone is told that all seats are in use. Nobody already signed in is affected.

What happens when the licence ends? Agents and administrators see a notice before it ends. A paid licence has a grace period during which calls keep working. After that, softphones already open keep working and calls are never cut, but new softphone windows cannot start until a new licence is installed. See the licence guide.

Does the licence need internet access to OctaveBytes? No. It is checked on your server only.

docs.title: Administration
docs.text:
Who can change settings? People invited to the admin console as administrators. Read-only people can look but not change.

Do settings changes affect calls in progress? No. A call keeps the settings it started with. Changes apply from the next call.

Can we switch the connector off quickly? Yes. Switch off Connector switched on in the console (Settings, Advanced) and save. Every call panel disappears within about a minute and GoHighLevel's own dialler works again. Calls in progress finish and are logged.

We forgot to press Save. Is that a problem? Nothing changes for agents until Save changes is pressed. The console marks unsaved changes and warns before you leave.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: How do we get help? Email support@octavebytes.com. Never send passwords, tokens, licence files, recovery codes or patient details.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

The addresses the connector server answers on, for network, firewall and security reviews. All are served through nginx over HTTPS on the connector's address. These endpoints serve the call panel, the softphone window and the admin console. They are not a general-purpose API for other systems, and their request and response shapes may change between releases. The WebSocket messages are described in the protocol summary.

Common behaviour: responses are JSON with ok and, on failure, a code and a plain message. Nothing is cached (Cache-Control: no-store). Security headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) are sent on every response. Browser requests from an origin that is not allowed are refused with 403.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

How the connector is built: components, data flow and trust boundaries. For security commitments see security and privacy.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Component Runs in Role Loader (loader.js) GoHighLevel pages (agency Custom JS) Loads the call panel from the connector's address. Call panel (bar.js) GoHighLevel pages, in its own isolated part of the page (Shadow DOM) Draws the panel, reads the GoHighLevel session proof, intercepts click-to-call, shows transcript, suggestions and summary. Holds no secrets. Built from shared packages plus a thin GoHighLevel shell. Softphone window (engine.html) A separate browser window on the connector's address Hosts the Amazon Connect softphone (Amazon Connect Streams), reports call state, carries out call commands (accept, dial, hold, mute, digits, wrap-up). The voice stays between this window and Amazon Connect. Connector server (backend/server.js, Node.js) Your server, behind nginx Signs agents in, relays messages between panels and softphone windows, enforces settings, looks up and writes GoHighLevel records, reads Contact Lens and Amazon Q. Serves the panel, the softphone page and the admin console. Connector core (packages/connector-core) Inside the server CRM-independent logic: call records and the write queue, the relay, sign-in tokens, AI feeds, wrap-up rules. GoHighLevel adapter (backend/crm/ghl.js) Inside the server Every GoHighLevel API call. The only part that knows GoHighLevel's API. Amazon Connect sources (backend/connect/) Inside the server Contact Lens (transcript, sentiment, summary) and Amazon Q in Connect. Platform (backend/platform/ and packages/) Inside the server, only when PLATFORM=on Licence check, seat counting, settings store, administrator sign-in, admin API and admin console. nginx Your server HTTPS, certificate, WebSocket upgrade, forwarding to the local port.

docs.title: Data flow: an inbound call
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Caller
  participant AC as Amazon Connect
  participant E as Softphone window
  participant S as Connector server
  participant P as Call panel (GoHighLevel page)
  participant G as GoHighLevel API
  C->>AC: calls your number
  AC->>E: contact rings (Streams)
  E->>S: STATE (incoming, number)
  S->>G: find contact by phone (create if unknown and allowed)
  S->>P: STATE + MATCH (caller card, screen pop)
  P->>S: ACCEPT
  S->>E: ACCEPT (only if allowed)
  E->>AC: accept
  S->>AC: poll Contact Lens and Amazon Q during the call
  S->>P: PANEL transcript / assist
  E->>S: STATE (ended, wrap-up)
  P->>S: WRAPUP (disposition, note) then COMPLETE
  S->>G: note, "Call completed" entry, comments (each written once, retried)
  S->>AC: fetch post-call summary
  S->>G: AI summary (comment, note, fields)
  S->>P: LOGGED, SAVED

Outbound calls follow the same path in reverse: the panel sends DIAL, the server checks the agent may dial and forwards it to the softphone window.

docs.title: Identity and sessions
docs.text:
1. The call panel asks GoHighLevel for the signed-in user's session proof (encrypted by GoHighLevel for the Marketplace app) and sends it to /v2/session.
  2. The server decrypts it with the app's shared secret, checks the sub-account, and looks the email up in the agent mapping. It returns a panel token (15 minutes, renewed every 10 minutes). The agent's room is their Amazon Connect user name.
  3. Open softphone asks /v2/engine-launch for a one-time launch token (60 seconds), placed in the softphone window's address. The window exchanges it for a softphone token at /v2/engine-session and renews it at /v2/engine-refresh. A softphone session ends after SESSION_MAX_HOURS (default 12).
  4. When Amazon Connect signs in inside the softphone window, the server checks that the Amazon Connect user is the one mapped to the agent; otherwise the window is closed.
  5. With the platform on, the softphone window takes a seat when its connection opens, confirms it when the Amazon Connect user is verified, and keeps it with a heartbeat every 20 seconds.

Panel, softphone and console tokens are signed separately and cannot stand in for one another.

docs.title: Trust boundaries
docs.text: Boundary What crosses it Controls GoHighLevel page ↔ connector Session proof, commands, call state, caller details HTTPS; allowed origins only (GoHighLevel domains, own address, ALLOWED_ORIGINS); signed short-lived tokens; agent mapping; rate limits. The panel runs inside GoHighLevel pages, so other scripts on those pages are outside our control. Softphone window ↔ connector Call state, commands Same as above, plus one softphone per agent and the Amazon Connect user check. Softphone window ↔ Amazon Connect Voice, softphone sign-in Amazon Connect's own security; the connector's address must be an approved origin. Connector ↔ GoHighLevel API Contact lookups, notes, call entries, comments, fields HTTPS; Private Integration token and Marketplace app token kept on the server only. Connector ↔ AWS Contact status, Contact Lens results, Amazon Q HTTPS; IAM role or key with the least-privilege policy in deploy/iam-policy.json. Administrator ↔ admin console Settings, seats, licence, accounts HTTPS only; passkey or authenticator code; roles; confirm-it-is-you for sensitive actions; same-origin requests only; no cookies. OctaveBytes ↔ your server Nothing at run time Licence file and public keys delivered by you; no network connection to OctaveBytes. Server ↔ disk Call records, tokens, accounts, audit File permissions for the service user; disk encryption is your responsibility.

docs.title: Settings enforcement
docs.text: Every switch an administrator can change is answered by the server at the moment it acts (for example, the relay refuses MUTE when mute is off), and is also sent to the panel so it can hide the control. A call keeps the logging settings it started with. The list of enforcement points per setting is in the settings reference.

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text:
• Write queue: each part of a call record stores the id GoHighLevel returns; retries, late wrap-ups and restarts skip parts already written. Retries run for about three hours (15 seconds doubling to a 10-minute cap). Unfinished records live in data/pending.json; the last 500 finished calls in data/ledger.json.
  • Reconnects: the panel and softphone window reconnect by themselves and resend their state; the server replays the latest state to a panel that reconnects.
  • Softphone lost: if a softphone window disappears during a call, the server closes the call and writes it after 5 minutes.
  • Single process: rooms and seats live in one server process (seats are also saved to disk). There is no high-availability mode in this release.

docs.title: Built from shared packages
docs.text: The server and the panel are assembled from packages in this repository, written in strict TypeScript and tested separately: core, audit, protocol, licensing, settings, admin-auth, admin-auth-webauthn, admin-api, admin-ui, seat-transports, connector-core, call-engine, bar-core, bar-state, skins, transports. The only third-party runtime library in the platform packages is SimpleWebAuthn (passkeys). Adding another CRM is described in the integration guide.

docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

Every place the connector keeps data, what it holds and for how long. Paths are under /opt/ob-ghl-connector/backend/ unless stated. "Retention" means automatic deletion by the connector. Anything without it is kept until you delete it. Summary for non-technical readers: security and privacy.

docs.title: In memory only
docs.text:
• Caller card details (cached for about 15 seconds), the live call state per agent, live Amazon Q suggestions and Ask Q answers, console sessions.
  • The live transcript, when PERSIST_TRANSCRIPT=off.

A restart clears these. Agents' panels and softphones reconnect and the state is rebuilt from the softphone.

docs.title: In the agent's browser
docs.text:
Where What Call panel storage (localStorage on the GoHighLevel address) Panel open or folded, full or compact view, chosen outbound queue, auto-refresh on or off Softphone window (sessionStorage) The softphone token (until the window closes) Admin console (sessionStorage on the connector address) The console session token (survives a page reload, cleared when the tab closes)

No cookies are set by the connector.

docs.title: In GoHighLevel (your account)
docs.text: Depending on the settings: the note, the "Call completed" entry with the recording link, the transcript comment, the AI summary comment, and the contact fields "Last call summary" and "Last call sentiment". Contacts created for unknown callers (tagged so they can be found). These are kept and deleted under your GoHighLevel account's rules. GHL_AI_TEXT=off stops every AI-produced text from being written there.

docs.title: In Amazon Connect (your account)
docs.text: Recordings, Contact Lens analysis (transcript, sentiment, summary) and Amazon Q sessions are created and kept by Amazon Connect under your instance's settings. The connector only reads them.

docs.title: At OctaveBytes
docs.text: Nothing from your installation. OctaveBytes keeps a record of the licences it issued to you (organisation name, location id, seats, dates).

docs.title: Deleting data for a person
docs.text:
1. GoHighLevel: delete or edit the contact's notes, comments and fields there.
  2. Amazon Connect: delete recordings and analysis under your storage rules.
  3. Connector server: there is no per-person delete in this release. Use RETENTION_DAYS, or remove the matching lines from data/calls.jsonl and the files in data/transcripts/ and data/summaries/ named after the call id, with the service stopped. The audit log holds no personal data.

docs.title: Integration guide: adding a CRM adapter
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

For engineers who need to see where another CRM would plug in. Release v2.0.0 ships one CRM, GoHighLevel. The guide describes the seams that exist in the code today. It does not promise support for other CRMs.

docs.title: The idea
docs.text:
The connector core (packages/connector-core) knows nothing about any CRM or page. A product supplies three things: 1. a CRM adapter on the server: single lookups and writes against the CRM's API; 2. a host shell in the browser: how the call panel reads the CRM page (who is signed in, which record is open, the CRM's own call buttons); 3. a product manifest: name, licence binding, and the settings an administrator can change.

The core owns everything else: the write queue and retries, the relay and rooms, tokens, wrap-up rules, AI feeds, licence and seats.

flowchart LR
  subgraph Server
    CORE["connector-core<br/>(queue, relay, auth, AI, wrap-up)"]
    ADP["CRM adapter<br/>(CrmAdapter port)"]
    POL["Policy<br/>(settings → core questions)"]
    PLAT["Platform<br/>(licence, seats, settings, admin)"]
  end
  subgraph Browser
    BAR["bar-core<br/>(call panel)"]
    SHELL["Host shell<br/>(HostShell port)"]
  end
  CORE --> ADP --> CRM[(CRM API)]
  POL --> CORE
  PLAT --> POL
  BAR --> SHELL --> PAGE[CRM page]

docs.title: 1. The CRM adapter port
docs.text:
Defined in packages/connector-core/src/adapter.ts (CrmAdapter). The GoHighLevel implementation is backend/crm/ghl.js. All GoHighLevel API calls live there.

Method Purpose id, labels(), bindings() Adapter name, words for messages (contact, sub-account), licence binding values (for example the account id). capabilities() What this CRM can do: call entry, note, timeline text, recording link and player, summary fields, screen pop, click-to-call, unknown-caller create, multi-match chooser, disposition ids. Settings that need a missing capability are refused. identify(proof) Checks the CRM's proof of the signed-in user and the account; returns the user or a reason. mapAgent(user) The telephony user name for this person, or null (the agent mapping). findByPhone, create, card Contact lookup, creation for unknown callers, caller card data. logCall, upsertNote, addTimelineText, appendNote, setSummaryFields The writes for one call. Each returns the id the CRM gave, which the core stores so a retry never writes twice. recordUrl, locationId, trustedDomains Links to records, the account scope for the panel, and the web domains allowed to call the server. health() Token and installation state for /health.

Rules for an adapter: one call per write (no own retries; the core retries). Throw on failure. Never touch telephony. Never log personal data.

A fake adapter with switchable failures (createFakeAdapter in packages/connector-core/src/fake-adapter.ts) is used by the core's tests and is the model to test a new adapter against.

docs.title: 2. The policy
docs.text: packages/connector-core/src/policy.ts lists the questions the core asks at the moment it acts (may this agent dial? is wrap-up on? which dispositions? write the note?). It contains no setting names. A product maps its settings onto these questions. For GoHighLevel that is backend/platform/policy.js. A call keeps the logging answers it started with.

docs.title: 3. The host shell port
docs.text:
Defined in packages/bar-core/src/shell.ts (HostShell). The GoHighLevel shell is shells/ghl/shell.js. It provides: the server's address and the CRM's name. Small storage. The session proof. The account and page kind. A self-test of the page elements it relies on. The open record. Safe page refresh. Opening a record. Intercepting the CRM's own call buttons (onDialRequest). And opening the softphone window synchronously (pop-up blockers).

The call panel (packages/bar-core), its state rules (packages/bar-state), the colours (packages/skins) and the connection (packages/transports) are shared. tools/gen-bar-bundle.mjs builds bundle/bar.js from them plus the shell; npm run check fails if the committed bundle is out of date.

docs.title: 4. The product manifest
docs.text:
backend/platform/manifest.js declares the product id, name, licence bindings, and every setting: key (namespaced platform.*, connect.* or crm.*, never renamed once released), section, type, label, default, parent, required capabilities, and the enforcement points. @octavebytes/core validates it at start. The settings reference is generated from it.

Every setting must be enforced on the server and covered by a test: settingsCoverage (from @octavebytes/settings) fails the build when a setting has no enforcement test (backend/tests/enforcement.test.js).

docs.title: 5. Rules the build enforces
docs.text: npm run check (tools/check-rules.mjs, rules in tools/rules.json) fails when: - a platform package names a CRM or telephony vendor, reads process.env, imports connector code, or depends on a package it is not allowed to; - the code sends or handles a message missing from the protocol catalogue; - a generated file (protocol reference, softphone bundle, call panel bundle, settings reference) is out of date; - a customer document quotes a setting key that does not exist, or a link in the documentation does not resolve.

docs.title: 6. Checklist for a new CRM
docs.text:
1. Write the adapter against CrmAdapter; test it with the core's queue and the fake adapter's failure cases.
  2. Write the host shell against HostShell; keep the page hooks behind selfTest().
  3. Write the manifest and the policy mapping; add an enforcement test per setting.
  4. Add a skin if the CRM needs its own colours.
  5. Build the panel bundle with the new shell; run npm run verify and the connector tests.

docs.title: Protocol summary
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

A short guide to the messages between the call panel, the connector server and the softphone window. The complete, generated reference with every field is protocol.md. It is generated from the code and checked on every build.

docs.title: Transport
docs.text:
• One secure WebSocket per browser page: wss://<connector address>/relay?role=bar|engine&token=<token>. bar is the call panel, engine is the softphone window. A panel token cannot open a softphone connection and the other way round.
  • Messages are JSON text frames with a type field. Protocol version 1.
  • The server pings every 20 seconds and drops connections that do not answer. Clients reconnect by themselves with increasing pauses.
  • Inside the softphone window, the page and the Amazon Connect frame exchange the same shapes with window.postMessage.

docs.title: Message families
docs.text:
Direction Messages Purpose Softphone → server STATE, HB, RELEASE Call and agent state (patches the server merges), seat heartbeat, deliberate log-out. Server → softphone CMD, ALREADY_OPEN, IDENTITY_MISMATCH, SEAT_RELEASED, CONFIG Commands from the panel; refusals; seat ended; current settings. Panel → server CMD, WRAPUP, ASK, ASSIST_FEEDBACK Commands for the softphone; disposition and note; questions and feedback for Amazon Q. Server → panel STATE, PRESENCE, MATCH, PANEL, LOGGED, SAVED, NOTICE, NO_ENGINE, SEAT_RELEASED, CONFIG Merged call state; whether a softphone is connected; caller lookup; panel tabs (caller, transcript, assist, summary); write results; short notices.

Commands inside CMD: DIAL, ACCEPT, REJECT, HANGUP, MUTE, HOLD, RESUME, DTMF, SET_STATE, COMPLETE, REPORT_STATE. The server forwards a command only to the agent's verified softphone, and only if the settings allow it.

docs.title: Close codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 4403 The Amazon Connect user in the softphone is not the agent the connection belongs to. 4409 A second softphone window for the same agent was refused. 4410 The seat was released (administrator, replaced, expired) or no seat was free.

docs.title: Notes on status
docs.text:
• HELLO (version negotiation) is defined but planned; the server does not use it yet.
  • CONFIG is sent by the server when the platform is on, although the catalogue still marks it planned (a correction is pending; see the release notes).
  • SIMULATE_INCOMING is a development aid; the server ignores it unless it runs in development mode.

Changing the protocol: messages are defined only in packages/protocol/src/catalog.ts; npm run docs regenerates protocol.md, and npm run check fails if the code sends or handles a message the catalogue does not list.

docs.title: Message protocol
docs.text:
Protocol version 1. Messages are JSON text frames on the WebSocket between call bar, relay server and engine (wss://host/relay?role=bar|engine&token=...). The engine page also forwards a STATE patch to the relay with window.postMessage({nhFrom:"engine", state}) and receives commands as window.postMessage({nhTo:"engine", ...cmd}); those local hops carry the same shapes.

Rules: every message is an object with a string type. Extra fields are allowed and ignored (a newer client must not break an older server). planned messages are part of the platform design and are refused by the validator until they go live.

docs.title: Engine to server
docs.text: Type Status What it is Fields STATE live The engine reports a patch of its state (see STATE_FIELDS). The server merges patches and replays the merged state to bars. state (object; required; state patch) HELLO planned First message on a socket: protocol version and client kind, so versions can be negotiated. v (number; required)client (string; required; up to 50 characters) HB live Engine heartbeat for the seat lease: proves the page is running and carries the agent status text and whether a call is in progress. Sent about every 20 s. The server treats a malformed one as no heartbeat. agentState (string or null; optional; up to 100 characters; the status name only (for example Available); not the object that STATE carries)call (string; optional; one of idle, on-call; on-call while any call or after-call work is open; this is what keeps the seat through a network drop) RELEASE live The agent chose to log out: the seat is freed at once. Closing the window instead keeps the seat for a short reconnect grace. none

Sent by a bar, forwarded unchanged by the server to the verified engine. cmd (object; required; one of COMMANDS) ALREADY_OPEN live A second softphone window for the same agent was refused; the engine must stop (socket closes with 4409). none IDENTITY_MISMATCH live The Connect user in this softphone is not the agent the room belongs to (socket closes with 4403). expected (string; required; up to 200 characters; the agent the window should be signed in as) CONFIG planned Effective admin settings, sent on connect and whenever they change. rev (number; required)config (object; required) SEAT_RELEASED live The session's seat was released (admin action, expiry or stale). The client must stop and say why. reason (string; required; one of admin, stale, licence, replaced)

docs.title: Release notes
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

Changes to the connector, newest first.

docs.title: v2.0.0: first release
docs.text:
New - Admin console at /admin/: settings for calling, wrap-up, conversation logging, AI assist and advanced options; Agents page with the seat meter and force logout; Licence page; Change history; Administrators; My sign-in. Works at phone width with a dark theme. Unsaved-changes marker, Save and Discard bar, warning before leaving with unsaved changes, conflict handling between two administrators. - Sign-in without passwords for administrators: passkeys and authenticator apps, a one-time setup code per installation, ten recovery codes, lockout after five failures, confirm-it-is-you for sensitive actions, read-only role. - Licence and seats: an offline signed licence bound to the GoHighLevel sub-account; one seat per open softphone window; grace period for paid licences; 15-minute call protection after a dropped connection; plain notices to agents and administrators. - Every setting enforced on the server, including required disposition and note, separate inbound and outbound disposition lists, and switches for each part of what is written to GoHighLevel. A call keeps the settings it started with. - Recording player switch: the "Call completed" entry with or without the recording player. - Platform install script (deploy/install-platform.sh) and the first-administrator setup code command.

Improved - The connector was rebuilt on shared, separately tested packages (call records and write queue, relay, softphone logic, AI feeds, call panel). Behaviour is unchanged: a differential check showed the softphone logic sends the same 65 messages as before, and 21 recorded call-panel scenarios match. - A call whose softphone window vanished (browser closed, laptop died) is now closed and logged after 5 minutes; previously it could be lost. - After a server restart, a returning softphone gets its old seat back. - The call history keeps call order under load. - Privacy and security hardening carried into this release: masked phone numbers and email addresses in logs, an audit log with ids only, retention controls, minimum-necessary switches, session lifetimes, webhook signature checking, security headers and rate limits, alerts, checksum-verified update packages, a least-privilege AWS policy and instance-role mode.

Fixed - The softphone window looped between "refused to connect" and the Amazon Connect sign-in screen, or showed "Camera is not accessible". The softphone page now sends Referrer-Policy: strict-origin and no longer blocks the camera (troubleshooting).

Known limitations - Call transfer and AI disposition suggestion are not available (shown as Planned). - One server process per installation; no high-availability mode. - With AWS_AUTH=role, the "Call completed" entry does not wait for Amazon Connect to finish saving the recording, so the player can show 0:00 until the page is reloaded. - The protocol reference still lists the CONFIG message as planned although the server sends it when the platform is on. - There is no per-person delete of call records on the server; use the retention setting.

docs.title: Before v2.0.0
docs.text: The earlier build was the GoHighLevel connector without the platform: softphone in GoHighLevel, screen pop and caller card, call logging, live transcript, Amazon Q assist and AI summary, supervisor monitoring support, and the privacy hardening listed above. It ran on the OctaveBytes test system from 20 October 2026.

docs.title: Agent guide
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

How to take and place calls from GoHighLevel. Your administrator may have switched some features off. If a button described here is missing, that is why. One page summary: quick reference card.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Use Google Chrome on your computer, with a headset.
  • Your administrator must have linked your GoHighLevel user to your Amazon Connect user. If not, the panel says "your email is not linked to an Amazon Connect agent. Ask your administrator to add you."
  • Allow pop-ups for GoHighLevel. If they are blocked, the panel says "Allow pop-ups for this site, then try again."

docs.title: 1. Sign in and open the softphone
docs.text:
1. Sign in to GoHighLevel as usual. The call panel appears on the right of every page: a small bar at the right edge (the mini bar) or the open panel. The coloured dot shows your state.
  2. Open the panel (click the mini bar, or the green «). If the panel says "Softphone window is not open.", click Open softphone.
  3. A new window opens: the softphone window. Sign in to Amazon Connect there with your Amazon Connect user name and password, and allow the microphone when asked.
  4. Keep the softphone window open all day. You can move it aside or minimise it, but do not close it: closing it ends your phone and frees your seat. If you try to close it during a call, the browser asks you to confirm.
  5. Back in GoHighLevel the panel shows your status, for example Available.

Only one softphone window per person can be open. A second one shows "The softphone is already open in another window or computer. Close this one."

If your organisation has used all its seats, the softphone shows "No softphone seat is free right now. Ask a colleague to log out, or ask your administrator for more seats." Try again when a colleague has closed their softphone.

docs.title: 2. The call panel
docs.text:
Part What it is Mini bar The folded panel at the right edge: status dot, your status or the caller, a timer, and Accept / Decline / Hang up when there is a call. Click it to open the panel. » handle Folds the panel away. Status pill Your Amazon Connect status and how long you have had it. Click it to change status. ▭ button Switches between the full view (all tabs) and the compact view (call controls only). Your choice is remembered. Caller card Who is calling: name, owner, last interaction and open deals from GoHighLevel. Tabs Call (controls), Assist (Amazon Q), Transcript (live words and sentiment), Summary (AI summary after the call).

The panel opens by itself when a call rings and folds away after the call, unless you opened it yourself.

Figure: The call panel folded to its mini bar, status Available (sample data).

Figure: The call panel open on the Call tab, idle (sample data).

Figure: The compact view during a call (sample data).

docs.title: 3. Status
docs.text:
Click the status pill and choose a status under "Set your status" (for example Available, Offline or a break). The list comes from your Amazon Connect setup. You cannot change status during a call ("Status changes after the call").

Choose Available to receive calls. Your status in the panel and in Amazon Connect are the same thing.

Figure: The status menu (sample data).

docs.title: 4. Answer a call
docs.text:
1. The panel opens and shows "Incoming call" with the number or the contact's name. The caller's contact usually opens in GoHighLevel at the same time (screen pop). For a number with no contact, a contact named "Unknown caller" with the number may be created for you to rename.
  2. Click Accept to answer, or Decline.
  3. If you do not answer, the call shows as "Missed call" and Amazon Connect stops sending you calls. Choose Available to take calls again ("Set to unavailable by a missed call. Choose Available to resume.").

Figure: An incoming call with the caller card (sample data).

docs.title: 5. Place a call
docs.text:
• From a contact: click the phone icon on the contact page or next to a number in the contacts list. The call goes through Amazon Connect, not GoHighLevel's own dialler.
  • By number: on the Call tab, type the number in the box and click Call. Include the country code for numbers abroad (for example +44 for the UK); local numbers use your organisation's default country.
  • Queue: if "Call from queue" is shown, choose the outbound queue before dialling.
  • Redial: under "Recent calls", click Redial next to a call.

Messages you may see: "Enter a phone number.", "That number is too short.", "That is not a valid international number.", "Finish the current call before dialling." If calling is switched off for your team: "Calling is switched off by your administrator."

docs.title: 6. During a call
docs.text:
Button What it does Hold / Resume Puts the caller on hold and back. The panel shows "Holding…" or "Resuming…" until Amazon Connect confirms. Mute / Unmute Stops the caller hearing you. A mute made in the softphone window shows here too. Keypad Opens a keypad to send digits, for example to an automated menu. Hang up Ends the call.

Transcript tab: the conversation appears within seconds, with who said what and the caller's sentiment (Positive, Neutral, Negative). Scroll up to read back; "New messages ↓" takes you to the latest.

Assist tab: Amazon Q suggests answers when the caller asks a question. Mark a suggestion Helpful or Not helpful, or click Copy to copy the answer. Type your own question in "Ask Q a question…" during a call.

If the transcript or Amazon Q is unavailable, the tab says so and adds "The call is not affected."

Figure: On a call, with Hold, Mute, Keypad and Hang up (sample data).

Figure: The Transcript tab with sentiment (sample data).

Figure: The Assist tab with Amazon Q answers (sample data).

Figure: A call on hold (sample data).

docs.title: 7. Wrap-up
docs.text:
After the call the panel shows "Call ended" and a wrap-up step: 1. Choose the outcome in Disposition…. 2. Type a note if you want (Notes (optional)). 3. Click Save & Done. Amazon Connect ends the wrap-up and you can take the next call.

Your administrator may require a disposition or a note. The panel will not finish wrap-up without them. The list of dispositions can differ for inbound and outbound calls.

Figure: Wrap-up with a disposition and notes (sample data).

docs.title: 8. What is saved to the contact
docs.text:
The panel shows "Logging to GHL…", then "Logged to GHL". A few seconds later a green strip says "Saved to GHL" with a Refresh button and an Auto-refresh switch. If auto-refresh is on and you are not typing or on a call, the contact page refreshes by itself ("Refreshing to show the saved call…", with Cancel) so you see the new note.

Depending on your organisation's settings, the contact receives: - a note with the call details, your disposition and note, the recording link and the AI summary; - a "Call completed" entry in the conversation, with the recording player; - the call transcript as an internal comment; - the AI summary as a comment and in the contact's "Last call summary" and "Last call sentiment" fields.

The Summary tab shows "Generating summary…", then the summary and where it was saved. Very short calls get no summary. If the summary could not be made, the tab says so. The rest of the call record is not affected.

If GoHighLevel cannot be reached, the panel says "Not logged yet, retrying:" and the server keeps trying. You do not need to do anything. The call is written once when GoHighLevel is back.

Figure: The "Saved to GHL" strip (sample data).

Figure: The Summary tab (sample data).

Figure: The note the connector writes on the contact (sample data).

Figure: The "Call completed" entry with the recording player, and the phone icon for calling from the contact (sample data).

docs.title: 9. Recent calls
docs.text: When you are not on a call, the Call tab lists your recent calls with the contact or number, and Redial.

The browser blocked the softphone window. Allow pop-ups for GoHighLevel in Chrome, then click Open softphone again. Reconnecting… / Reconnecting to the server… The connection to the server dropped. docs.title: Good practice
docs.text:
• Lock your computer when you leave it: the panel shows caller details.
  • Do not share your GoHighLevel or Amazon Connect sign-in.
  • Close the softphone window at the end of the day, so the seat is free for others.

docs.title: Quick reference card
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

A one-page summary for agents. Full guide: agent guide.

Start of day 1. Sign in to GoHighLevel in Chrome. 2. Open the call panel (right edge) → Open softphone → sign in to Amazon Connect in the new window, allow the microphone. 3. Keep the softphone window open. Set your status to Available.

Calls

To… Do this Answer / refuse Accept / Decline Call a contact Click the phone icon on the contact page or in the contacts list Call a number Call tab → type the number (+country code for abroad) → Call Call again Recent calls → Redial Hold Hold, then Resume Mute Mute, then Unmute Send digits Keypad End Hang up Finish Choose Disposition…, add a note, Save & Done Change status Click the status pill (not during a call) Fold the panel » (open again from the mini bar) Compact or full view ▭ button in the panel header

During the call: Transcript shows the words and sentiment; Assist shows Amazon Q suggestions and Ask Q. Summary fills in after the call.

After the call: "Logged to GHL" then "Saved to GHL". The contact page refreshes by itself when safe.

If you see… - "Softphone window is not open." → Open softphone - "Allow pop-ups for this site…" → allow pop-ups for GoHighLevel, try again - "Reconnecting…" → wait; the call continues - "Missed call" → choose Available to take calls again - "No softphone seat is free right now…" → try later or ask your administrator - "…already open in another window or computer…" → use your open softphone window

End of day: close the softphone window so the seat is free. Lock your computer when you leave it.

docs.title: Supervisor guide
docs.text:
Document version 1.0 · 25 October 2026 · Applies to release v2.0.0

What supervisors can do with release v2.0.0. The connector does not add its own supervisor screens: live monitoring uses Amazon Connect's own tools, and the connector works alongside them. Team leads who also manage settings or seats use the admin guide.

docs.title: Listen in and barge in (Amazon Connect)
docs.text:
Status: Available.

What you need (your Amazon Connect administrator sets this up): - a security profile that allows real-time metrics, real-time contact monitoring and barge-in, and access to the Contact Control Panel; - if your instance limits monitoring by agent hierarchy, you must be in the agent's hierarchy group or above; - enhanced monitoring (multi-party calls) switched on for voice in the instance.

Steps: 1. Use your own browser session (another Chrome profile or a private window), never the agent's. 2. Sign in to Amazon Connect, allow the microphone, open the Contact Control Panel (phone icon, top right) and set yourself Available. Without an open, Available panel, listen-in is accepted but nothing connects. 3. Go to Analytics and optimisation → Real-time metrics → Agents, find the agent ("On contact"), and click the eye icon on the voice line. 4. Your panel shows Monitoring mode: Monitor (silent). To speak, change the mode to Barge. Leave call exits.

What the connector does meanwhile: - The agent's call panel shows nothing extra during silent monitoring (monitoring must stay silent). During barge the agent and the caller simply hear you. - The call is logged once, on the customer's contact, with the customer's number. No extra contact, note or call entry is created for your connection. - If you also use the call panel yourself and you are the one monitoring, your panel shows "Monitoring a call" and your monitoring is not logged as a call.

docs.title: See who is on the phone (admin console)
docs.text: If you have an admin console account (full or read-only), the Agents page shows who has the softphone open, their status, whether they are on a call, when they signed in and when they were last seen, with the seat count. See the admin guide.

docs.title: Review calls afterwards
docs.text: Every call leaves a note, a "Call completed" entry with the recording player, the transcript comment and the AI summary on the contact in GoHighLevel, depending on your organisation's settings. The recording plays for people signed in to Amazon Connect with permission to hear recordings.

docs.title: Not in this release
docs.text: There is no supervisor dashboard, call whisper, call transfer or reporting inside the call panel. Use Amazon Connect's real-time and historical metrics.
